newsitem.title: UK: Euro straight-run fuel prices rise on good demand.
newsitem.headline: Euro straight-run fuel prices rise on good demand.

text.p: European straight-run fuel oil prices firmed on Wednesday to catch up with crude's rise and take account of a well-priced cargo deal, traders said.
An Irish refiner was heard to have sold to a European refiner late on Tuesday for a price around $106 fob a tonne.
It was the third cargo trade in the first two days of the week, as refiners scrambled to purchase alternatives to newly expensive crude.

Bids were heard at $104 fob and offer levels were $106-$107 a tonne in northwest Europe. But sellers were still complaining that straight-run was undervalued compared to crude, despite Wednesday's 30 cent drop in Brent futures.
Availability is now thin until late May or early June.
Baltic Russian material was very scarce, and what little appears was attracting a premium, traders said. M-100 material was heard worth two means plus $6 or $7.
But in the Mediterranean some 100,000 tonnes of straight-run was due to appear in ports in the next few days, with neither bunker nor refinery buyers showing much interest.
The opening up of the Russian inland waterways was believed to have sparked a flood of poorer quality material that could find few outlets.
